items.lesson_concept: Personal Information includes data which, when put together with other information, would directly and certainly identify an individual[cite: 1].
items.question_text: An anonymous corporate survey collects only the 'Department', 'Years of Experience', and 'Exact Salary' of employees without asking for names. In a small startup of 15 people, these three data points point exclusively to the single Lead Developer. Under the DPA, how is this dataset classified?
options: It is strictly Anonymized Data because the 'Name' field was omitted.
It is Personal Information, because when put together, the information directly and certainly identifies a specific individual.
It is Privileged Information because it involves salary details.
It is Public Domain Information because surveys are voluntary.
items.correct_answer: It is Personal Information, because when put together, the information directly and certainly identifies a specific individual.
items.explanation: Even if a name is omitted, if the collected data points, when combined, can reasonably and directly ascertain an individual's identity, it is classified as Personal Information[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Sensitive Personal Information includes data about a proceeding for any offense committed or alleged to have been committed by an individual[cite: 1].
items.question_text: An HR department requires a job applicant to submit a court clearance detailing an ongoing, unresolved lawsuit where the applicant is falsely accused of theft. The applicant argues this data should not be used for hiring. How does the DPA classify the data in this court clearance?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Public Domain Information
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
items.explanation: Information relating to any proceeding for an offense committed or even just alleged to have been committed is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) under the DPA[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: A Personal Information Processor (PIP) acts only on the documented instructions of the PIC[cite: 1]. If they deviate, they assume the role and liabilities of a PIC.
items.question_text: A marketing agency (PIP) is hired by a retail brand (PIC) to process a customer mailing list strictly for sending holiday discounts. The agency decides, without telling the brand, to use the same list to promote their own separate software product. What is the legal consequence of the agency's action?
options: The agency remains a PIP but must pay a minor penalty to the retail brand.
The agency unlawfully assumes the role of a Personal Information Controller (PIC) by independently deciding a new purpose and means for processing the data.
The retail brand is solely liable because they collected the data initially.
The agency is protected as long as their software product is legitimate.
items.correct_answer: The agency unlawfully assumes the role of a Personal Information Controller (PIC) by independently deciding a new purpose and means for processing the data.
items.explanation: Because a PIP acts strictly on the documented instructions of the PIC[cite: 1], unilaterally deciding a new purpose for the data strips them of their PIP status and makes them a PIC engaging in unauthorized processing.

items.lesson_concept: PICs carry legal accountability for personal data under their custody, even when outsourced, and must bind PIPs via formal agreements[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A bank outsources its entire customer service operations to an offshore call center, signing a contract stating the call center assumes '100% of all legal privacy liabilities'. If the call center leaks the data, how does the DPA view the bank's accountability?
options: The bank is completely absolved of liability because of the signed contract.
The bank retains accountability for the data under its custody and cannot contractually waive its ultimate responsibility under the DPA.
The bank is only liable if the call center is located within the Philippines.
The bank and the call center automatically become Joint Controllers.
items.correct_answer: The bank retains accountability for the data under its custody and cannot contractually waive its ultimate responsibility under the DPA.
items.explanation: Under the principle of accountability, the PIC remains legally accountable for personal data under its control, even when processing has been outsourced to a third-party PIP[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Information about an individual's education is classified as Sensitive Personal Information[cite: 1].
items.question_text: An online platform allows users to upload their high school and college transcripts to connect with potential tutors. The platform suffers a breach and the transcripts are leaked. Given the specific data involved, what level of breach occurred?
options: A breach of General Personal Information.
A breach of Sensitive Personal Information (SPI), since education records are classified as SPI.
A breach of Privileged Information.
A standard security incident with no privacy implications.
items.correct_answer: A breach of Sensitive Personal Information (SPI), since education records are classified as SPI.
items.explanation: Section 3(l) of the DPA explicitly categorizes personal information about an individual's education as Sensitive Personal Information[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Privileged Information refers to data constituting privileged communication under the Rules of Court[cite: 1].
items.question_text: The CEO of a company communicates via a secure messaging app with the company's in-house legal counsel regarding an impending corporate lawsuit. A rogue IT admin intercepts these messages. What classification protects this specific data?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Public Domain Information
items.correct_answer: Privileged Information
items.explanation: Attorney-client communications are protected under the Rules of Court, rendering the data involved as Privileged Information under the DPA[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: A PIC is a person or organization who controls the collection, holding, processing, or use of personal information[cite: 1]. When multiple entities jointly make these decisions, they are joint controllers.
items.question_text: A ride-sharing app and a fast-food chain launch a joint promotional campaign. They sign an agreement to pool their customer databases, jointly deciding to run a machine learning algorithm to find overlapping customers for targeted ads. What is their specific role in this arrangement?
options: The ride-sharing app is the PIC and the fast-food chain is the PIP.
They act as Joint Personal Information Controllers because they jointly determine the purpose and means of the processing.
They act as Joint Personal Information Processors.
They are both completely exempt under the commercial marketing exception.
items.correct_answer: They act as Joint Personal Information Controllers because they jointly determine the purpose and means of the processing.
items.explanation: Because both entities collaboratively control the collection, use, and processing (deciding what data is used and why), they share the role of Personal Information Controller[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: SPI includes data issued by government agencies peculiar to an individual (e.g., SSS, GSIS, TIN, Passport Number)[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A building security guard requires all visitors to surrender their driver's licenses and records the unique license numbers in a logbook before granting entry. What is the legal classification of the recorded license numbers?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Anonymized Information
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
items.explanation: A driver's license is an ID issued by a government agency peculiar to an individual, making it Sensitive Personal Information under Section 3(l)[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: A Data Subject is an individual whose personal, sensitive personal, or privileged information is being processed[cite: 1]. Juridical persons are not data subjects.
items.question_text: A massive B2B database leaks the corporate tax identification numbers (TIN) and registered office addresses of 5,000 registered corporations (Inc. and Corp.). Can the affected corporations file a privacy complaint claiming their rights as 'Data Subjects' were violated?
options: Yes, corporations possess the exact same privacy rights as human beings.
No, the term 'Data Subject' strictly applies to individuals (natural persons), not juridical entities like corporations.
Yes, provided the corporations are 100% Filipino-owned.
No, because tax identification numbers are public domain.
items.correct_answer: No, the term 'Data Subject' strictly applies to individuals (natural persons), not juridical entities like corporations.
items.explanation: A Data Subject refers specifically to an individual (a living human or natural person) whose information is processed, explicitly excluding corporate or juridical entities[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: CCTV footage capturing identifiable faces is Personal Information[cite: 1]. Processing includes collection, recording, and storage.
items.question_text: A neighborhood association installs a CCTV camera pointing at a public street. The camera actively records faces but the footage automatically deletes every 24 hours without anyone ever watching it. Is the association 'processing' Personal Information?
options: No, because the footage is deleted before anyone views it.
Yes, because recording and temporarily storing CCTV footage of identifiable faces constitutes the processing of Personal Information.
No, because public streets are exempt from the DPA.
Yes, but it is classified as Privileged Information.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because recording and temporarily storing CCTV footage of identifiable faces constitutes the processing of Personal Information.
items.explanation: CCTV footage capturing identifiable faces is explicitly Personal Information, and the acts of collecting, recording, and storing it—even temporarily—constitute processing[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: A PIP acts only on the documented instructions of the PIC[cite: 1].
items.question_text: An IT vendor (PIP) experiences a server overload while processing a client's (PIC) data. To prevent downtime, the vendor quickly transfers the data to a secondary subcontractor cloud service without informing the client. Did the vendor violate their DPA obligations?
options: No, because ensuring server uptime is an implied contractual right of any IT vendor.
Yes, because a PIP must act only on the documented instructions of the PIC, and subcontracting requires prior authorization.
No, provided the subcontractor is located in the Philippines.
Yes, but only if the subcontractor suffers a data breach.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because a PIP must act only on the documented instructions of the PIC, and subcontracting requires prior authorization.
items.explanation: Because a PIP acts strictly on the documented instructions of the PIC, they cannot unilaterally transfer data to a new subcontractor without the PIC's explicit authorization[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: SPI includes data about an individual's religious, philosophical, or political affiliations[cite: 1].
items.question_text: An online forum requires users to declare whether they identify as 'Atheist', 'Agnostic', or 'Religious' to participate in certain debate boards. How is this specific data field classified under the DPA?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Public Domain Information
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
items.explanation: Information concerning an individual's religious or philosophical affiliations is explicitly categorized as Sensitive Personal Information (SPI) under Section 3(l)[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: The PIC carries legal accountability for the data. The DPO is designated to ensure compliance, but the corporate entity/officers bear the ultimate legal penalties for breaches[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A corporation suffers a massive data breach due to gross negligence by the Board of Directors, who ignored the Data Protection Officer's (DPO) repeated warnings. When the NPC investigates, does the DPO bear the ultimate criminal liability for the breach?
options: Yes, the DPO is always strictly liable for any breach under their watch.
No, the Personal Information Controller (the corporation and its responsible officers) carries the ultimate legal accountability for the data, especially since they ignored the DPO.
Yes, because DPOs are required to physically secure servers.
No, liability is transferred entirely to the hackers.
items.correct_answer: No, the Personal Information Controller (the corporation and its responsible officers) carries the ultimate legal accountability for the data, especially since they ignored the DPO.
items.explanation: While the DPO is accountable for overseeing compliance, the PIC (the organization and its responsible officers) holds the ultimate legal accountability and faces the penalties for the data under its custody[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: SPI includes information about an individual's race, ethnic origin, or color[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A cosmetics company collects data on the exact skin color and ethnic background of its customers to provide personalized makeup recommendations. What classification does this data fall under, requiring stricter processing rules?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Commercial Information
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
items.explanation: Data concerning an individual's color, race, or ethnic origin is strictly classified as Sensitive Personal Information under Section 3(l)[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Processing includes the erasure or destruction of personal data.
items.question_text: A company purchases second-hand hard drives and discovers they are full of the previous owner's customer data. The company immediately runs a military-grade wipe to destroy the data. Did the company 'process' the data by wiping it?
options: No, destroying data means it was never processed.
Yes, because the legal definition of 'processing' explicitly includes the erasure or destruction of personal data.
No, because the company did not own the data.
Yes, but only if they read the files first.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because the legal definition of 'processing' explicitly includes the erasure or destruction of personal data.
items.explanation: The DPA's definition of processing covers the entire lifecycle of data handling, specifically including operations like erasure or destruction[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Personal Information is data from which identity can be reasonably and directly ascertained[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A whistleblower leaks a spreadsheet containing only employee job titles and exact hire dates, with all names removed. In a 50,000-employee company, these exact combinations uniquely identify 10 specific senior executives. Does this spreadsheet contain Personal Information?
options: No, because the names are absent, making it fully anonymized.
Yes, because the identity of the individuals can be reasonably and directly ascertained from the specific combination of data points.
No, job titles and hire dates are strictly public domain.
Yes, but only if the executives complain.
items.correct_answer: Yes, because the identity of the individuals can be reasonably and directly ascertained from the specific combination of data points.
items.explanation: If the data points provided, when put together, allow the identity of an individual to be reasonably and directly ascertained, it constitutes Personal Information, even without a name[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: SPI explicitly includes an individual's 'age'[cite: 1].
items.question_text: An online forum asks users to input their exact 'Age' (e.g., 34) rather than a general birth year to determine access to age-restricted boards. Under the strict definitions of Section 3(l), how is this data point classified?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Anonymized Data
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
items.explanation: Section 3(l) of the Data Privacy Act explicitly lists an individual's 'age' as Sensitive Personal Information[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: PICs must bind third-party processors (PIPs) via formal data sharing or outsourcing agreements to maintain security[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A hospital (PIC) hires an external developer to build a patient portal but only signs a standard 'Service Level Agreement' covering payment terms and uptime, with no clauses regarding data protection. Why is the hospital non-compliant with its PIC obligations?
options: The hospital should have hired a government developer.
The PIC failed to bind the PIP via formal outsourcing agreements that mandate adequate data security measures.
The developer must be registered as a PIC first.
Service Level Agreements automatically cover data privacy by default.
items.correct_answer: The PIC failed to bind the PIP via formal outsourcing agreements that mandate adequate data security measures.
items.explanation: A core obligation of accountability is that a PIC must use formal contractual controls (like a Data Processing Agreement) to ensure their PIPs maintain adequate security measures[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: Information about an individual's sexual life is classified as Sensitive Personal Information[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A dating application collects detailed user preferences regarding their sexual orientation and lifestyle to improve algorithmic matchmaking. What level of data classification applies to this information?
options: General Personal Information
Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
Privileged Information
Public Information
items.correct_answer: Sensitive Personal Information (SPI)
items.explanation: Data regarding an individual's sexual life or orientation is explicitly classified as Sensitive Personal Information under the DPA, requiring stricter processing safeguards[cite: 1].

items.lesson_concept: A PIC decides what data is collected and why. A PIP processes on the PIC's behalf[cite: 1].
items.question_text: A multinational retail brand uses a third-party email service provider (like MailChimp) to send newsletters. The email provider requires the brand to upload customer emails, but the provider's terms state they will never use the emails for their own purposes. Who is the PIC?
options: The email service provider is the PIC.
The retail brand is the PIC, as they control the collection and determine the purpose of the mailing list.
Both are Joint Controllers.
The customers are the PICs.
items.correct_answer: The retail brand is the PIC, as they control the collection and determine the purpose of the mailing list.
items.explanation: Because the retail brand controls the collection, holding, and purpose of the data, they are the PIC. The email service provider merely acts on their instructions as a PIP[cite: 1].
